videos.title_guess: The Closing Room – November 2026 (Tom Hegna: Holiday momentum, grandparent annuity/life strategies, ethics, asking questions)
videos.summary: Weekly 'Closing Room' agent training hosted by annuity.com CEO Brett Blake with guest Tom Hegna (ex-military, former New York Life annuity trainer, PBS/CNBC retirement educator, author of Paychecks and Playchecks and Don't Worry, Retire Happy). Hegna presents holiday-season ideas: December is the top month for life/annuity production; use family gatherings for family financial meetings; pitch grandparents a joint-life SPIA with a grandchild (birthday checks, 50% death benefit, potentially ~$2.6M of payouts on $100K) or a 10-pay whole life/IUL on a grandchild; a 'five lifetimes, one annuity' successor-owner SPIA structure; a list of holiday outreach ideas (widows/widowers, early-60s Social Security/Roth/QLAC/RMD/IRMAA conversations, term conversions, age-change/birthday deadlines, rated policies, centers of influence, client gifts, Valentine's lunch for widows). Q&A covers running family meetings (use AI to build agenda), joint annuities with ex-spouses, how to answer 'are you a fiduciary?', new-agent mistakes (talking too much, asking too few questions), starting late on retirement, AUM advisors and annuity conflicts, and handling 'call me in January'. Brett also tells of a Find-an-Agent MYGA lead on annuity.com that closed a $200K MYGA and relays a Matthew Allen point that Social Security is typically a ~$1M asset.

terms_definitions.definition: Annuity funded with one premium that begins income right away; can be written joint-life on two people (e.g., grandparent + grandchild). Not available as a fixed index annuity.
Income annuity whose payments start at a future date; can also be used for the grandparent/grandchild structure.
A SPIA that accepts newborn/young annuitants; many SPIAs require age 18+. Needed for grandparent-grandchild joint-life contracts.
SPIA option that, upon the death of the last annuitant, pays 50% of the original premium to a beneficiary; the death benefit portion is treated as return of principal (tax-free) per Hegna.
Method by which part of each SPIA payment is treated as tax-free return of principal.
Person named to take over ownership/income checks of an annuity at the owner's death; enables 'five lifetimes, one annuity'. If not exercised, the young joint annuitant receives the checks.
Permanent life policy (whole life, IUL, GUL) where premiums are paid for 10 years then policy is paid up; used for grandchild gifting.

Fixed annuity with guaranteed rate for a term; competes with CDs. Hegna's 'triple interest': principal earns interest, interest earns interest, and money that would have gone to taxes earns interest (tax deferral).
Required Minimum Distribution; Hegna says to begin planning conversations in client's 60s before RMDs start at 73.
Qualified Longevity Annuity Contract; mentioned as 60s-age planning topic.
Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount; Medicare surcharge; RMDs can raise it and increase taxation of Social Security.
Converting a term life policy to permanent coverage; holiday outreach idea because term premiums rise annually.
Hegna's phrase: life insurance and annuities pass directly to beneficiaries without a trust.

Obligation to act in client's best interest; enforced only through lawsuits—no monitoring body checks fiduciaries. Selling only one product type is inconsistent with being a fiduciary (7-iron golf analogy).
Advisors paid on AUM may avoid recommending annuities/longevity products; Hegna notes annuities with fee options now exist so commissions aren't required.

claims_stats.claim: December is always the #1 month for life insurance and annuity production (company/MDRT year-end).

A joint-life SPIA with 50% death benefit can potentially pay out about $2.6M on a $100,000 premium across grandparent, grandchild and great-grandchild (Hegna illustration; New York Life contract; inflation option).
Great-grandchild would receive $50,000 tax-free on a $100,000 premium with 50% death benefit (Hegna).
Fewer than 1% of agents know the five-lifetimes-one-annuity structure (Hegna's estimate).
Joint SPIA payout is based on the younger annuitant's age, so payout rate is lower.
Hegna's 12-pay whole life premium was $226,000/yr; he put in about $2.3M and cash value is about $3.8M (year 15–16).
Hegna saved 30–40% of income for his whole career and says he has paid no interest in 35+ years.
Research cited by Brett: roughly 60–70% of people plan to change financial advisor after death of a spouse or parent.
Per Matthew Allen (via Brett): Social Security is often a ~$1M+ asset; $2,500–$2,800/mo per person, ~$3,500/mo couple would take almost $1M in an immediate annuity to replace (Hegna).
An annuity.com agent closed a $200K MYGA from a Find-an-Agent page lead from Florida.
Fidelity sells billions of annuities and its AUM rose after it did (Hegna).
Don't Worry, Retire Happy story: newly divorced woman at 55 with almost nothing retired at 71 with more income than ever by saving heavily, delaying Social Security and working to 71.

sales_teachings.teaching: Hold a family financial meeting during holidays
sales_teachings.detail: Gather the whole family; agents lose business when the breadwinner dies because spouse/children weren't engaged. Use Claude/Grok to generate agenda/15 questions; ask parents what they want to accomplish and permission to call the children; act as facilitator/'quarterback'; whiteboard issues; bring in specialists later.

Have client try listing four grandparents and eight great-grandparents (can't); contrast with Rockefeller descendants who get annual trust checks. Propose joint-life SPIA with 5-year-old granddaughter paying on her birthday.
Solve for $100K/$250K/$500K/$1M at age 65; show premiums; policy accessible earlier for college/home down payment (no 59½ rule); grandfather can write a love note in the policy.
Joint life grandpa + granddaughter; chain successor owners grandma→son→son's wife→granddaughter.

Call widows/widowers (lonely); early-60s for SS/Roth/QLAC/RMD/IRMAA; IRA/401(k) rollovers; term conversions; age-change birthdays (Oct–Feb); rated/smoker policy re-underwrites; centers of influence (attorneys, CPAs, clergy); deliver small gifts in person; Valentine's lunch for widows/widowers.
Give specific urgent reasons: upcoming birthday raising premiums, family coming to town, rising costs with age; and keep other holiday prospects in the pipeline.

sales_teachings.teaching: Show whole life/IUL isn't more expensive
sales_teachings.detail: For permanent insurance, premiums stay in the policy as cash value; aim for highest premium, not cheapest.
New agents' biggest mistake is talking too much. 'Find problems, solve problems.' Don't be an 'annuity retailer'; let the client talk themselves into needing an annuity.

Reframe: 'I always do what's best for you regardless of label'; point out fiduciary is enforced only by lawsuits, and one-product agents or no-annuity AUM advisors aren't truly serving best interest. (Compliance caveat: Brett noted 'aside from the obvious compliance'.)

sales_teachings.teaching: Always do what's best for the client
sales_teachings.detail: Hegna says he out-earned colleagues by ignoring commission schedules; trust drives referrals.
MYGA leads (CD season) can open the relationship; sell the MYGA then broaden to portfolio conversation.

sales_teachings.teaching: Reassure late starters via Social Security as base
sales_teachings.detail: Tell prospects they already own a ~$1M Social Security asset as a base to build on; show real dollar cost of replacing via immediate annuity quotes.
New agents can identify problems in meetings and bring back questions to the annuity.com community rather than force answers.

notable_quotes.quote: Telling is not selling. Listening is selling. Asking questions is selling.
Find problems, solve problems. Be a good problem finder and be a good problem solver.
You don't have to sell annuities. The annuities will sell themselves.
Trust is the most valuable thing you can have with your clients.
Always do what's best for the client. You'll always make the most money in your office.
Five lifetimes, one annuity.
I would just say I do what's best for the client, doesn't matter fiduciary, not fiduciary.
There's nobody out there enforcing fiduciary rules. You know how fiduciaries enforced? Through lawsuits.
MYGAs, multi-year guaranteed annuities pay triple interest. Your principal earns interest, your interest earns interest, and the money you would have paid in taxes earns interest.
MIGA is can be the doorway you walk into to gain that trust and access to everything else. [unclear: 'MIGA' = MYGA]

videos.title_guess: The Agent Opportunity – November 2026 (Brett Blake: Reinventing Retirement Distribution)
videos.summary: Brett Blake's weekly (Wednesday) recruiting presentation 'Joining us in reinventing retirement distribution.' Pitches annuity.com as a technology company reinventing annuity distribution rather than another IMO fighting for the same ~100,000 producing agents. Frames retirement distribution as broken (retirees afraid to spend; 'mountain of money' vs 'river of money'), sizes the market (~$2.3T annual guaranteed-income opportunity; annuity sales $219B→$464B since COVID), and lays out a four-phase intelligence roadmap using FedEx hub-and-spoke and Amazon analogies: (1) hub-and-spoke referral from Medicare agents/CPAs; (2) Policy Intelligence System; (3) Portfolio Intelligence System; (4) Marketing Intelligence System. Shares progress (900+ enrolled, 800+ licensed, ~430 carrier-contracted; 80+ carriers), and 'top seven' reasons to join: full street commission day one, uncapped/cap-the-company, real equity, free tech (AI licensing prep, guaranteed income sheet), free concierge case management, lead programs (Medicare/RAMP, seminars, Lead Pro with leads now delivered free), no-lock-in release guarantee. Describes Lead Pro bundle at $199, training cadence, brand claims, and joinannuity enrollment. Ends with Q&A from a new agent about annuity training.

notable_quotes.quote: We really fundamentally believe that retirement distribution is broken and it needs to be fixed and our goal is to use technology and use new systems to reinvent it entirely.

Research shows that when you can actually help them convert that pile of money into or the mountain of money into a river of money, and they know that they have a guaranteed income... something happens. Their retirement changes.
It's like trying to drain a modern dam with an old Roman aqueduct.
We are a technology company. We are a company reinventing distribution.
We have full street commission from day one. We don't take your commission to feed your upline.
Instead of capping you, we cap our earnings on every agent every year.
Every other IMO wants you to build their company. We'd rather you own ours.
We're the only consumer brand in the annuity space and for sure the only consumer brand IMO in the industry.

Unlike other IMO's where if you sign up you're stuck, you have to go sit on the sidelines for six months before you can get released. We guarantee our new agents that if you aren't happy... we're going to release you. No questions asked.
Nothing about the house has changed, but the agents become better.

videos.summary: Training webinar announcing annuity.com's partnership with Social Security Advisors (SSA-alumni advisory firm, owners of irma.com) and featuring CEO Matthew Allen. Brett introduces the partnership (back office for agents; liability shifted to SSA-advisors; IRMAA 2027 follow-up Dec 9, 10am PT). Allen covers: why ~70% of Americans leave money on the table (~$120K per couple, $25B/yr); complexity (2,728 rules, 9,200+ strategies); SSA legally can't give advice; core basics (top 35 years, age 62/FRA 67/70, 8% delayed credits); can vs. should claim; deemed filing; married strategies (higher/lower earner rules of thumb, time value of money, spousal vs survivor benefits, voluntary suspension); divorced spouse rules (10-yr marriage, independent entitlement after 2 yrs); survivor benefits (OIG found 82% misinformation, John & Susan $221K example, 'survivor surprise'); singles 'rat holes'; business owner S-corp payroll tax tactic; retroactive benefits; reliance and trust fund 2032 projection; earnings test ($24,480 for 2026); Social Security Fairness Act (WEP/GPO repeal, retroactive to Jan 2024); family/child/disability benefits; withdrawal of application; four ways to file; IRMAA appeals and life-changing events; and the service/fee schedule and free tools (chat widget, co-branded consult links). Strong definitional/SEO content.

terms_definitions.definition: Age at which unreduced retirement benefit is available; 67 for anyone born 1960 or later (66 for those born 1943–1954).
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: 62 for retirement benefits; survivors may claim as early as 60 (50 if disabled).
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Benefit grows about 8% per year (2/3 of 1% per month) after FRA up to age 70; benefit at 62 ≈ 75% of FRA amount; at 70 historically up to 132% (now ≈124% for those born 1960+).
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Formula SSA uses to compute benefit from highest 35 years of earnings; has three bend points (A, B, C); in bracket C only ~15 cents on each additional dollar is credited.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Benefits are based on a worker's 35 highest-earning years.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Filing a standard application is treated as applying for every benefit you may be eligible for, which can cause loss of benefits (esp. spousal and survivor cases); can be avoided in certain cases (restricted application).
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Extra benefit available to lower earner based on higher earner's record without reducing the higher earner's benefit; requires higher earner to have filed in married couples.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Benefit paid to widow/widower; higher earner's claiming decision sets the ceiling; survivor generally gets the higher of the two benefits, not both ('survivor surprise').
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Survivors discover they can only keep the higher of two benefits (not both) when a spouse dies.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: After FRA, a person can pause benefits to restart delayed retirement credits (8%/yr, monthly); dependents' benefits also suspend; benefits auto-resume at 70. Distinct from repealed 'file and suspend' (ended by Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015).
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: After being divorced at least 2 years, and if ex-spouse is eligible age (typically 62), a divorced spouse can claim on the ex's record even if the ex hasn't filed; marriage must have lasted 10+ years.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: If under FRA and claiming, SSA withholds $1 of benefits per $2 earned above the limit ($24,480 in 2026 per Allen); test ends at FRA; withheld amounts are later re-credited via adjustment for reduction factor.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: If over FRA, a lump sum up to 6 months of back benefits can be claimed; reopening for SSA error can reach back to age 70.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Within 1 year of claiming a person can withdraw once to fix a mistake.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Windfall Elimination Provision / Government Pension Offset—negative rules reducing SS for people with non-covered pensions (teachers, police, firefighters); repealed by Social Security Fairness Act.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Benefit for child disabled before 22.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Benefit for a spouse caring for an eligible child.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Claiming ages for singles that fall into PIA formula dips: 62 to 63 and 11 months, and 65 and 4 months to 66 and 8 months—generally avoid.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Higher Medicare premiums for higher earners, based on income from two years prior; can be appealed after life-changing events (marriage, divorce, death of spouse, work stoppage, work reduction, loss of income-producing property).
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Overpaid Medicare premiums that may be recovered via IRMAA appeal even retroactively in the same year.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.definition: Disability expected to prevent work for at least a year, with work in 2 of last 5 years (per Allen).
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

terms_definitions.term: Four things to do with Social Security money
terms_definitions.definition: Spend, invest, pay down debt (all with time value), or—not recommended—park in non-interest checking.
terms_definitions.source_video: txVBQNelyZs_Maximizing Your Client’s Social Security with Matthew Allen.en.txt

synthesis:
Batch synthesis.
1) Company vs educational. COMPANY content: videos 2–4 (Agent Opportunity Nov 2026, Opportunity Call Apr 2026, undated Agent Opportunity) are annuity.com recruiting pitches by CEO Brett Blake; videos 3 and 4 are near-duplicates (same script; undated one adds Amy's Fast Start $100 Lead Pro reimbursement) so dedupe when generating pages. Core company facts that recur: pre-release letter, 100% street commission from day one, cap-the-company at $5M, agency builder (7 degrees), real restricted stock ($1K/$4K/$10K at $1M/$3M/$5M), no lock-in, Lead Pro bundle, RAMP Medicare pathway, seminar pathway (Roy Snarr, Bill Broach), concierge, Tom Hegna on demand, sole consumer-brand IMO claim. Numbers changed over time: April 2026 says 800+ agents, 60+ carriers/2,400+ products, Lead Pro written '$1.99' (caption error, most likely $199); Nov 2026 says 900+ enrolled/800+ licensed/~430 contracted, 80+ carriers, Lead Pro $199, free company-acquired leads starting to flow, 4-phase intelligence roadmap. Use latest (Nov 2026) numbers; flag Lead Pro price and carrier/product counts as time-sensitive.
2) EDUCATIONAL content is concentrated in video 5 (Social Security with Matthew Allen) and in Tom Hegna's Closing Room (video 1). The Social Security video yields ~20 definitions (FRA, delayed retirement credits, deemed filing, spousal vs survivor, voluntary suspension, independent entitlement, earnings test, PIA/bend points, WEP/GPO, retroactive benefits, IRMAA) suitable as glossary/FAQ/long-form SEO pages, with worked numeric examples (John & Susan $221K; S-corp payroll tax $15,300→$4,590). Caveats: figures are 2026-specific (earnings test $24,480; 2032 trust-fund projection) and must be verified against SSA before publishing; Allen's views (trust fund fixes, 100% taxation) are opinion; some rules (e.g., divorce-decree provisions, 'rat holes' ages, 85% taxation) should be fact-checked. Social Security Advisors pricing is partner company information, not annuity.com's.
3) Cross-video links. (a) Hegna's early-60s outreach (SS, Roth, QLAC, RMD, IRMAA) is exactly what the Allen partnership operationalizes; Brett relays Allen's 'SS is a ~$1M asset' framing as a confidence-building opener, and Hegna's immediate-annuity-quote method prices that asset (~$3,500/mo couple ≈ nearly $1M). Allen explicitly connects annuities to SS: fill the cash-flow gap while delaying, survivor-surprise protection, and lead generation via chat widget. (b) 'Find problems, solve problems' (Hegna) parallels Allen's qualitative-question approach and the new-agent 'appointment setter→fact finder' ladder in the opportunity calls. (c) Trust/brand theme: Brett 'trust usually found in a brand; no trusted annuity brand', Hegna 'trust is the most valuable thing', MYGA as doorway, Find-an-Agent MYGA lead case study. (d) Agent-first ethics: transparent pay, no commission skimming (video 3/4), vs Hegna's 'do what's best for client' and fiduciary skepticism.
4) SEO/marketing reuse ideas: MYGA 'triple interest' explainer; grandparent legacy annuity/10-pay life gifting; 'five lifetimes one annuity' (flag as advanced/carrier-dependent; Hegna's tax and payout claims need carrier/CPA verification); survivor benefits and 'survivor surprise'; IRMAA appeal guides ahead of Dec 9 session; Social Security Fairness Act retroactive claims; S-corp payroll tax and SS benefits; fiduciary myth content; 'why agents leave IMOs' and pre-release letter pages.
5) Caption artifacts: 'IRMA' = IRMAA; 'MIGA' = MYGA; 'nudity.com'/'anuity.com' = annuity.com; 'Financialize/Financial I' partner name unclear; 'Leia' unclear; Lead Pro '$1.99' = likely $199; 'Roy Snar' = Roy Snarr; 'Bill Brooch' = Bill Broach; 'Brent' = Brett.
6) Compliance flags: Hegna's fiduciary talk, tax-free death benefit claims, and illustration figures; 'up to 70% more business', '5% = $100B', 'only consumer brand' are promotional claims; the 'real estate' comparison company is unnamed.
